finding: Honda's factory boost target is scaled by the pedal (less pedal targets less boost) and then ramped over time toward the table. Boost Target Ramp Rate (2 improved, 2 aggressive levels) shortens only the time ramp. On this car the target settles at a level set by the pedal: about 12.5-13.8 psi at TPS 41-46 and 15.0 psi at TPS 62, well under the 21 psi table. The 19.2 psi peak (aug30-1529) came with the pedal still rising (TPS 63-83).
ktuner_setting: Boost Target Ramp Rate (Quick Adjustments); Boost_Target_2_Normal_L/H
log_channel: Turbo Pressure Target vs TPS and Engine RPM
notes: Data: stage2/plateau.py found 12 windows (4 samples, target flat within 0.15 psi, TPS within 3, rpm >= 3,000): TPS 41-46 -> 12.0-13.8 psi; TPS 62 -> 15.0 psi at 3,080 rpm; TPS 92-94 -> 16.3 psi at 5,215-5,403 rpm. The card says the target "follows the pedal and climbs over seconds"; the nuance is that at a steady part pedal it stops at a pedal-set level, it does not keep climbing to the table. civicx-19 is a search summary.

finding: In KTuner logs TPS is the driver's pedal and TPS Command (TPS.C) is the throttle-plate command. KTuner staff: the pedal reading (TPS) is your foot on the pedal.
notes: Raises the boost-target-gap research inference (TPS = pedal, M) to a KTuner primary statement (raw ktuner-forum p9224, post 9217). Confirms that the engine gate "TPS Command >= 85 = full throttle" over-counts pulls, and that kc-boost-step is right to gate on TPS. Better category: logging-tunerview.

finding: On 10th-gen KTuner logs a floored pedal reads about 100-113 % TPS (KTuner staff: about 113 %; owners 100-104 % and 106 %). This car's TPS has never passed 94 % (6 samples on one drive, aug22-0903), so either the 11th-gen pedal stop reads near 94 or no logged pull was floored.
log_channel: TPS (key on, engine off, pedal floored); TPS on the proof pull
notes: kc-boost-step equates 'floored' with TPS >= 85 %, resting on the research reading that TPS 94 is the pedal stop. If the 11th-gen stop reads 100+ like the 10th gen, TPS 85-94 is part pedal and the proof pull could pass without a floored pedal. Settle with a key-on engine-off pedal-floor reading in TunerView. Fit caveat: 10th-gen scale; ktuner-forum-9 car generation not stated.

finding: KTuner keeps many factory protections in its Starter maps: an owner on Starter 21 Dual with the pedal at 106 % and TPS Command at 96 % never exceeded 19.5 psi, and KTuner's answer was a custom tune to get around those protections. A KTuner rep said 21 psi was chosen as a safe limit for CVT longevity.
ktuner_setting: none exposed (factory torque limiter / protections; not Final_Boost_Target, not Boost_By_Gear_Limits)
log_channel: Turbo Pressure Target on a floored pull held >= 5 s above 3,500 rpm, read against TPS and Engine RPM
notes: Conflict only as the explanation of our 19.2 psi: KTuner's protection cap (19.5 psi, floored) vs pedal scaling plus ramp on part-pedal pulls (our data, g1-boost-01). Both can be true: our logged pulls never floored the pedal long enough to meet the protection. The one near-floored moment held 16.3 psi at 5,200-5,400 rpm, which fits a protection at high rpm. Car generation in ktuner-forum-9 not stated; civicx-50 is a search summary.

finding: Some non-North-American CVT ECUs (EU 5AN-EKx) log TPS Command stuck near 95 % at full pedal with the boost target at 18-19 psi on a 21 psi dual map; an MT car on the same map logged 100 % and 21 psi. A 10th-gen CVT logged TPS Command 80-90 % against a 23 psi target until a KTuner beta build fixed it (cruise control lost). Not this car's signature: TPS Command reached 100 % (aug22-0903) and 99 % (aug30-1529).
log_channel: TPS Command max on a floored pull
notes: Refuted as the cause of our 19.2 psi gap, by data: stage2/tps.py. Keep as a diagnostic: if a floored held pull ever shows TPS Command pinned at 80-95 % with TPS at its stop, that is a KTuner support case (software build), not a map edit. civicx-66/67/29 are search summaries; civicx-67 also blames TCS/VSA for the 95 % cap (see g1-thr-09).

finding: With PID boost control a 1-2 psi overshoot is normal (22.8 psi on a 21 psi target); a 1-3 psi spike during the CVT's simulated shift at high rpm is normal; a single-sample spike where the target channel itself jumps (e.g. to -3.9) is a logging glitch. More aggressive Ramp, Responsiveness and Spool settings make overshoot more likely.
log_channel: Turbo Pressure minus Turbo Pressure Target, held >= 0.5 s; Turbo Pressure Target sanity (drop rows where it jumps with Turbo Pressure at -14)
notes: Our gate (overshoot <= 1.5) is stricter than KTuner's 'normal' 1-2 psi, so a healthy car can fail on a transient. Judge held overshoot, not single samples, and skip the simulated-shift moment. The boost-target-gap work already dropped two glitch rows of this kind (51.7 and 22.8 psi with boost -14). 10th-gen sources. civicx-20/28 search summaries.

finding: Final Boost Target takes the incoming target from the boost target table, the partial-throttle boost target or the Boost By Gear limit, passes it nearly one to one, and caps it at its last TBST column (KTuner's example: header 22 -> 22.5 max). To target more, the TBST header and that whole column must change. KTuner's 10th-gen Starter 21 default final target is 22.5 psi.
notes: Our map's top is 23.4 psi, every column >= 8.2 identical in every rpm row: it passes the target through and is not the 19.2 cap. The 'partial throttle boost target' input is the KTuner-documented name for the pedal scaling in g1-boost-01. civicxi-88 adds that the final table can override 'at your own risk'.

finding: Boost By Gear Limits is enabled on all Starter and editable maps: one limit table per gear, RPM by atmospheric pressure. It only limits: if the target is lower, the target table runs, so set it above the targets wherever it should not bite. Quick Boost By Gear offers flat 10-21 psi or ramped 10-20 psi (full above 4,000 rpm). KTuner does not set it for you; values around 33-35 psi mean not limiting.
ktuner_setting: Boost_By_Gear_Limits; Quick Boost By Gear Settings
notes: Our map: 35.4 psi in every cell, so not limiting (matches kc-table-boost). Open: which gear number a CVT presents to BBG; our logged Gear is the CVT step number (1-5 during pulls). civicx-7 says Starter tunes set no BBG limit by default, consistent.

finding: Owners and KTuner use Boost By Gear to cap first gear (about 12-18 psi, often ramped) for traction and to reduce stress on CVTs; KTuner says to set it whenever boost dampening is disabled on a CVT. Vendor tunes (TSP, Phearable) ship a low-speed or ramped first-gear limit.
notes: out-of-scope (context): the app does not write BBG (fix-spec "Out of this spec"). Per-gear ladders 12/14/18/20/21 are 6MT numbers, not ours. Use as the answer to "how do KTuner owners protect a CVT": a first-gear limit, never brake launches. civicx-7/54/64 search summaries.

finding: KTuner shows boost referenced to sea-level pressure, so at altitude the logged psi understates relative boost (16.7 psi shown at 4,200 ft is about 20 psi relative), targets go unmet at altitude, and the factory limit falls with atmospheric pressure. Owners use an ambient offset; KTuner warns timing and fuel must follow.
ktuner_setting: Turbo Pressure Limit Based On Atmospheric Pressure; ambient pressure offset
notes: Rules altitude out for our gap: Turbo Pressure reads -0.3 psi at 0 rpm on aug23-1959 (stage2/plateau.py), i.e. near sea level. civicx-77/78 search summaries.

finding: KTuner: the Honda ECU is target-torque based, not target-boost based; a value in the boost table does not guarantee that boost, the ECU adjusts to conditions, and on the Type R boost by gear is done by cutting Torque Targets Per Mode.
ktuner_setting: Torque Targets Per Mode (Type R only; not exposed on 22+ 1.5T)
log_channel: Turbo Pressure Target vs Boost_Target table
notes: Same Bosch logic as owner-voices row 11 ("the lowest limit wins"). T3 for the Type R page.

finding: Each map holds six boost target tables (three on-the-fly tunes x ECO and Normal). On the non-Si 1.5T, Boost Target - ECO runs in ECO and Boost Target - Normal in Normal and Sport (the Si has a Sport table instead). Starter 21 Dual Tune 2 = 18 psi ECO / 21 psi Normal-Sport; Dual Tune 1 keeps factory ECO. ECO off is needed for full boost.
log_channel: Turbo Pressure Target (above 18 psi proves Normal mode)
notes: Our aug30-1529 target 19.2 > 18 proves Normal there. civicxi-94 adds: set all three maps explicitly. civicx-29/51 search summaries.

finding: A stock 1.5T makes about 12-15 psi peak (owners' logs and a pro tuner's dyno; a stock Integra/Civic run hit 14 psi against a 16-18 psi target), so Starter 21 asks about 6-8 psi over stock.
notes: Expectation: our 19.2-19.9 psi is already 4-7 psi over stock. Mixed generations (10th gen non-Si, Integra).

finding: On 21 psi maps owners usually log 18-20 psi on the road (20 psi peak on Starter 21; an Si 2-3 psi short at peak; TSP Si maps 1-5 psi short), while others reach 21-23 with overshoot. KTuner's first checks for a target well under the map: the tune was not flashed properly, or Knock Control is pulling back; owners fixed some cases by re-flashing stock and redoing the install.
log_channel: Turbo Pressure Target, Knock Control at the peak
notes: Our checklist results: Knock Control 0.49-0.53 at every peak (not KC); target 19.2 > ECO 18 on aug30-1529, so the 21 psi Normal table is in the car (flashed). So 19.2 psi sits inside what owners see and is not a fault sign.

finding: Boost short of target with slow build then overshoot points to a pressure leak (couplers, O-rings after an intercooler install) or a failing wastegate actuator; KTuner asks for a datalog to support.
log_channel: Turbo Pressure vs Turbo Pressure Target with EWG Position and EWG Target
notes: Log reading: EWG nearly shut and boost still under target = leak or turbo limit; EWG open with boost under target = control/target side. Our car: boost tracks target, EWG 2.4-3.7 % at full load (no leak sign). Pairs with owner-voices row 9.

finding: Owners on custom tunes run 23-23.5 psi with 2-8 degrees more timing on 11th-gen 1.5T cars (China RON98; Turkey E5 FE1 CVT with downpipe, intercooler and CVT cooler: 100-200 km/h in 15.5 s); others run 21-22 psi on the Integra in cold weather and warn higher needs caution.
notes: out-of-scope (context): custom ignition plus RON98/E5 fuel. Not a contradiction of kc-table-ignition (its street rule is a judgement for our E10 RON95 car).

finding: KTuner staff: boost cut is set in psi, and Low/High boost tables follow the Low/High switch for boost control; Low/High cam ignition and fuel follow VTEC.
notes: T3. Our digitized note says 'L=Low cam / Low octane, H=High cam / High octane'; what selects L vs H on the 22+ 1.5T is unconfirmed. Harmless for the app because the Boost step writes L and H together.

finding: Ethanol Boost Target Adjustment is a TPS x RPM table that adds a percentage of boost to the final target.
notes: Our map holds 0 in every cell and no ethanol sensor is fitted, so it is not in play. It shows KTuner's boost-side tables can use a TPS (pedal) axis; the Normal table's unlabelled column axis may be pedal too (see conflicts-g1.md, 19.2 psi section).

finding: A 10th-gen CVT owner gave the factory map and the Starter dual map identical boost tables (ECO 16 / Normal 18) and they drove very differently (factory: more timing, slow response; Starter: less timing, quick boost): the Starter files carry settings beyond the boost tables.
notes: Supports 'never rebuild a Starter map by editing the factory file'.

finding: KTuner Quick Adjustments: Throttle Responsiveness (Factory, Improved levels, maybe an eco level), Turbo Responsiveness (spools faster to reach part-throttle targets; Partial Throttle Boost Response was merged into it), Turbo Spool (how hard the turbo chases the current target; never on Si), Boost Target Ramp Rate (high-throttle ramp), ECO Button, Throttle Padding (MT), Advanced VSA. Turbo Ramp options reached the 22+ 1.5T in 1.0.11.9. Turbo Responsiveness affects targeting and wastegate control only and does not lift target limits.
ktuner_setting: Throttle Responsiveness; Turbo Responsiveness; Turbo Spool; Boost Target Ramp Rate
log_channel: TPS, TPS Command, Turbo Pressure Target, EWG Position
notes: Nuance for kc-quick-adjustments: on a floored pull the time ramp is Boost Target Ramp Rate's job; Turbo Responsiveness works on part-throttle targets. Differences between Improved levels are subtle (youtube-12). civicx-41 search summary.

finding: Owners find Starter maps with aggressive Quick Adjustments livelier off the line and in the midrange than TSP Stage 1, but weaker at the top end; too much Early Spool plus part-throttle Turbo Responsiveness 'fizzles' up top. Common conservative picks are Improved II on throttle, spool, responsiveness and ramp; never disable the boost ramp.
notes: Expectation: Quick Adjustments change feel and low-end response, not peak power; it is taste, one change at a time. Mostly 10th-gen CVT owners. civicx-42 search summary.

finding: Disable Boost Target Dampening (Quick Enables) removes all factory dampening: above 15 % pedal the ECU always chases the boost table, the target never drops to atmospheric, and P0299 must be disabled. KTuner says to add Boost By Gear on a CVT if you use it; owners call it really harsh on the CVT, and with the ramp removed one 10th gen logged 24 psi on a 21 psi map.
log_channel: Turbo Pressure Target at TPS < 15 % (never atmospheric = dampening disabled)
notes: It is the only KTuner setting that lifts the part-pedal target, which is why it is tempting for our 19.2 psi question; for this CVT it stays off (KTuner's own CVT warning). no map change. civicx-21 search summary.

finding: Boost Target Ramp Rate improved levels (KTuner added them for the Integra and all 11th-gen Civics) bring boost in sooner and even out the curve around 4,500 rpm at both factory boost and 21 psi, on an owner's back-to-back logs.
log_channel: Turbo Pressure Target slope (psi/s) on matched floored pulls
notes: Integra manual car. Our logged ramp: about 1.6-2.5 psi/s at Factory Ramp. A Ramp level would show as a steeper target slope on a floored pull.

finding: Early Spool starts spooling sooner and adds low and mid range; KTuner says it pairs well with Part Throttle Turbo Responsiveness, does not cause overboost and won't hurt long term. One owner says Turbo Responsiveness only works fully with Early Spool on; another says Early Spool wears the turbo.
log_channel: Turbo Pressure vs Engine RPM on matched pulls (spool rpm)
notes: KTuner's help gives Turbo Responsiveness its own effect, so the 'needs Early Spool' claim is one owner's. The turbo-wear claim is opinion against KTuner's statement. Our card keeps Early Spool off for a different reason (low-rpm torque on the CVT, LSPI band): unaffected.

finding: Rev hang (throttle held open on lift, there for emissions) is removed with the Disable Rev Hang quick enable or Overrun Throttle Compensation (100 % = factory, 0 % = none); the code runs only at zero pedal above 2,000 rpm. It is not the fuel-cut delay. Tunes reduce it but some hang stays (electronic throttle, dual-mass flywheel).
ktuner_setting: Disable Rev Hang; Overrun Throttle Compensation
log_channel: Engine RPM after TPS returns to 0
notes: Mainly a manual-gearbox complaint. no map change (teach-only).

finding: Throttle Padding (Standard harshest, Medium, Soft nearest to stock) smooths the lift-off after Disable Rev Hang and exists only on manual-transmission cars.
notes: MT only.

finding: The pedal is never one-to-one with the throttle plate: by design the ECU opens the plate to help spool, and with high boost targets the plate opens near fully even at half pedal; on the DBW tables 83.3 % commanded is effectively fully open. Throttle and drivability settings are global across the three on-the-fly tunes, and Sport always feels sharper than Normal.
notes: Our data agrees: under boost TPS Command sits >= 20 points above TPS in 475 of 526 samples (boost-target-gap research). So TPS Command can never be the full-throttle gate. Also confirms kc-map-switching (throttle setting shared).

finding: Traction control (VSA) pulls the throttle back on a slip event, which costs boost and power in a pull; owners fully disable it for timed runs, and KTuner's Advanced VSA trades throttle pullback for ignition pullback. One owner blamed TCS/VSA for a 95 % throttle-command cap.
log_channel: TPS Command dropping while TPS holds; Speed vs Engine RPM
notes: A proof pull with a VSA event is void: TPS Command falls below its usual level while TPS stays at its stop. Not seen on our pulls so far (TPS Command stays above TPS). no map change.

finding: Low-rpm judder at 1,000-1,500 rpm and light throttle in 2nd came from the ECU oscillating the commanded throttle and was mostly fixed in KTuner 1.0.9.5/1.0.9.6.
log_channel: TPS Command oscillation at steady TPS, 1,000-1,500 rpm
notes: 10th gen; search summary.

finding: Idle speed is a Main Parameters option; raising it about 50 rpm cured an idle shake on a 2022 CVT, and Phearable idles its non-Si tune at 740 rpm (stock 600-700).
notes: civic11forum-82 also notes Starter 16.5 cannot run 87, no per-mode octane, auto start-stop delete possible. no map change (app does not write idle).

finding: On turbo Honda DBW the Final DBW table takes the standard table's output as its incoming throttle value, so Final and ECO should not match; DBW tables for every driving mode are exposed from 1.0.14.2 (CR-Z entry).
notes: Not exposed for our use; context only.

finding: Turbo lag on the 1.5T is substantial at low throttle; one owner says a turbo inlet pipe and turbo blanket helped more than the tune or the intake.
notes: Single Si owner.

finding: An Si owner on a Phearable 1.5R with an E85 blend saw Knock Control at 0.49 but misfires on all cylinders (unresolved).
notes: Better category: ignition-knock / fuel-octane.

finding: ECO Button options: Factory ECO Control, Normalized ECO (ECO feels like Normal but keeps economy traits) and Normalized ECO plus Sport+ Non-ECO.
notes: Throttle feel only; the ECO boost table is separate.

finding: KTuner's 22+ Civic 1.5T basemaps (Starter 16.5, 18, 1 Dual Tune 1/2, 21, 21 Dual Tune 1/2) all improve throttle response, remove low-end throttle dampening and reduce lag; KTuner asks 91+. Claimed gains: Starter 18 up to +30 whp / +38 lb-ft, Starter 21 up to +55 whp / +58 lb-ft, Dual Tune 2 ECO stage up to +30 whp / +40 lb-ft. (Si: Starter 21 +47 / +52, Flex +63 / +69.)
notes: kc-expectations carries the 58 lb-ft but not the +55 whp, and should label both as KTuner's claim. 'Removed throttle dampening on low end' does not mean the target is undamped above 3,500 rpm: our plateaus show pedal scaling there (g1-boost-01).

finding: Starter and vendor maps deliberately limit low-end torque on CVT cars for longevity (KTuner on the 22+ Civic CVT: 'We limit low end torque'); TSP limited non-Si output for the engine and CVT and softened the CVT Integra's torque; pro tuners cut torque below about 4,000 rpm; KTuner says to keep torque limited on a factory clutch or CVT even with a downpipe; full boost at low rpm in high gears (lugging) stresses the clutch.
notes: Data: our Normal tables cap 15 psi at 2,500, 17 at 2,750, 19 at 3,000 and reach 21 only from 3,500 rpm: the low-end limit is visible in the file. This is why the Boost step starts at 3,500 rpm and boost_raise_min_rpm is 3,000. civicx-16 search summary; civic11forum-106 is a manual-clutch note.

finding: Owners compare off-the-shelf tunes by feel: Starter maps feel livelier or jumpier down low, TSP and Phearable smoother and stronger at the top; an e-tune beats any off-the-shelf file for a specific car; Phearable can revise for extra mods.
notes: Subjective. civicx-63 search summary (0-60 0.25-0.5 s faster on KTuner Stage 2, TSP pulls harder above 4,000-5,000).

finding: On The Fly Map Switching is not supported on every ECU software number: TSP gives those cars the Map 3 file only and Phearable runs Level 3 all the time. KTuner's 22+ Civic 1.5T feature list marks it Full Support. TSP's Map 1 is the stock/valet map when the KTuner is unplugged.
log_channel: none (no tune channel); dash/V2 tune indicator after a long press of Cancel
notes: The Boost step relies on Tune 2. Before the first step, confirm switching works on this car's ECU (the three tunes are identical today, so no log can show it).

finding: KTuner tunes are tied to ECU part and software numbers: earlier-year files do not load on later ECUs; international 22+ ECUs marked * have only initial tuning support (an appointment to read the ECU); some international FE1 ECUs and the Australian ECU were not supported at all, and local file tuners there saw 0.8 bar against a 1.3 bar target.
notes: Record the owner's ECU part number against KTuner's 22+ list (raw ktuner-official site-22civicturbo). An international initial-support ECU is one more reason to expect factory protections to stay in place (g1-boost-04).

finding: Owner censuses: KTuner is on about 79 % of tuned 10th- and 11th-gen 1.5Ts; TSP Stage 1 is the most popular off-the-shelf tune; on 11th gens 35 % run base maps, 49 % off-the-shelf, 16 % custom.
notes: Self-reported surveys.

finding: KTuner basemaps are generic files built from a dyno-tuned similar setup; custom tuning gives better results; vendor tunes come with KTuner's base maps preloaded; KTuner had 22+ 1.5T base maps before the vendors.
The 22+ Civic 1.5T basemaps remove the speed limiter.
notes: Off-road note from KTuner; a safety line for the owner, not a tuning item.

finding: Si variants: Starter 21 Flex Fuel exists for the 22+ Si; on the Si the Starter 21 dual tunes put 21 psi in Sport and Dual Tune 2 puts 18 psi in Normal.
notes: Si only.

finding: An owner runs Starter 21 Dual 1 in winter and Dual 2 in summer and saw white smoke at WOT at 30 F (likely moisture).
notes: Cold climate.

finding: A Phearable 1.5R Race-MAF version reportedly reduced the artificial knock-control rise on hard pulls (16 CVT, PRL Cobra intake).
ktuner_setting: MAF Scaling; artificial knock control rise checkbox
notes: Better category: maf-airflow / ignition-knock. Search summary.

finding: KTuner updated existing 10th-gen maps for the 2018 oil-dilution recall.
notes: Better category: reliability-failures. Cold-climate issue.

finding: Vendor off-the-shelf layouts and boost levels: TSP non-Si Stage 1 Map 1 stock (valet) / Map 2 16.5 psi / Map 3 24 psi (16.5 in ECO); TSP Si and 10th gen Map 2 18-19 / 20-21 psi, Map 3 23-26 psi; Phearable levels about 15-16 / 20-23 / 24-25.5 psi (27.5 on E30); PRL big-turbo 26.4 psi; typical map 3 is near 250-260 hp on an Si.
ktuner_setting: On The Fly Map Switching (vendor files)
notes: Only TSP non-Si Stage 1 is our engine and gearbox; the rest is Si/Integra/10th gen. Confirms kc-boost-step: 24 psi is a vendor file (TSP Map 3), not a step. civicx-121 adds: self-tuning boost without timing and fuel is how rods break.

finding: Never launch, brake-boost or do burnouts in a tuned CVT; Phearable's own email says the CVT is fine with tunes but abuse makes it fail sooner; limit WOT pulls from a stop.
log_channel: Speed and Engine RPM at pull start (pull from a roll, not a stop)
notes: A transmission cooler only helps overheating (civic11forum-11).

finding: CVT fluid temperatures on 21-23 psi maps: about 77-90 C in normal use, 93-99 C after 20 min of freeway on an 11th gen (no failure reported), up to 108 C after an hour on a 10th gen until a cooler held it under about 93 C; another owner on 23 psi never passed 90 C.
notes: Our peak is 95 C (hot traffic). Owners pass 100 C without reported failure, which keeps our Stop 100 C provisional rather than measured. civicx-49/79 search summaries.

finding: Tuned-CVT owners change the fluid every 15-25k miles (24,000-40,000 km), the first change matters most; a hot-climate owner found the fluid cooked at 20k miles; a cooler is widely recommended.
notes: Search summaries; the 25,000-mile severe-service figure is quoted, not read in a Honda manual. Use as context next to 'severe schedule' in kc-cvt, labelled forum.

finding: The '250 Nm / lb-ft' CVT ceiling is folklore with no published limit; Hondata R&D reportedly tested the 1.5T CVT to 15 % over stock (about 260-280 wtq estimated) with belt burnishing but no reliability problem.
notes: Supports removing the torque number (kc-torque-250nm stays superseded). Search summaries.

finding: KTuner does not flash or change the transmission controller; CVT problems after a tune come from the engine's added demand, not a TCM change.
log_channel: Transmission Temperature; slip check (Engine RPM vs Speed)
notes: Answer for "did the flash change my CVT shifting / reverse engagement?".

finding: KTuner warns CVT cars make more torque on ethanol even without extra timing; custom tuning is recommended for flex fuel.
notes: E10 only here; no flex sensor.

finding: An owner on Starter 21 (94 octane) hears a little CVT whine after long spirited driving.
On a CVT, MAF-scale logging must sweep the curve and watch sensor voltage because a fixed gear can't be held (paddles help).
notes: Better category: maf-airflow.

finding: A stock 2022 non-Si 1.5T CVT makes about 154-164 whp and 163-165 lb-ft at the wheels (TSP 154/163; Hondata 164 whp at 4,263 rpm, 165 lb-ft); 11th-gen CVT dynos read far below 10th-gen manual dynos because the CVT loses more.
notes: Against the 176 hp crank rating that is about 7-13 % driveline loss, plausible for a CVT. civicx-18 adds a Phearable CVT review stock 182 whp / 194 wtq (10th gen).

finding: Off-the-shelf gains on a stock 11th-gen non-Si CVT: TSP Stage 1 191 whp / 227 lb-ft (from 154/163; up to +56 whp at 3,800 rpm); Phearable Stage 1.5 194 hp / 237 lb-ft, which Phearable says is +18 hp / +25 lb-ft over KTuner's 21 psi basemap. That implies Starter 21 near 176 whp / 212 lb-ft on Phearable's Dynojet. On a 10th-gen manual, Starter 21 made 203 whp / 250 lb-ft vs 187/200 stock.
notes: The implied Starter 21 figure is a competitor's arithmetic (194-18, 237-25), so plausible only. Phearable's own stock baseline is inconsistent across its pages (+60/+79 vs +38/+80). Torque gain (about +50-55 lb-ft) matches KTuner's +58 claim; the +55 whp claim looks high next to it. vendors-1 counted in g1-res-01 too.

finding: Si / Integra dyno results on stock-turbo tunes: TSP Stage 1 Si 241 whp / 286 lb-ft (from 196/190), Stage One+ 230/287, Stage 2 flex 254/308; Phearable Si 1.5 RACE 194-246 hp across levels, Stage 2.5 246/292 on 93 and 270/338 on E30; Integra KTuner 23 psi base 222 whp / 249 lb-ft (ECU reading about 22 psi) from 197/212; Hondata custom Si +28 lb-ft at 24 psi.
notes: Si (manual, more boost and fuel) numbers do not carry to our non-Si CVT.

finding: Big-turbo and flex builds on 11th gens make about 280-341 whp (PRL drop-in 308/304 on 93, 341/318 on E26; 27WON Gin 280/303 on 91, about 330/324 on E30; RV6-turbo 314/271 on race fuel; IMW remote E50 255/299).
notes: Big turbo / ethanol.

finding: Fuel economy after a tune stays about the same if driven gently (35-37 mpg average, 40s on the highway) and drops with a heavy foot; one owner fell to 18-20 mpg, and the advice was to flash back to stock to compare and check for a failed downpipe cat.
log_channel: STFT B1, LTFT B1 (a big economy drop with rich trims points at the cat or a sensor, not the tune)
notes: Expectation line; on E10 add the 3.4 % energy loss from kc-e10. Mixed generations, US fuel.

finding: Owner timings on tuned 1.5Ts: 0-60 mph about 5.6-6.1 s on Starter dual 21 (10th gen), under 6 s on Stage 1 base (10th gen, self-timed, vs about 7 s stock), 5.8 s with a short-ram intake; an Si ran 14.6 s quarter mile on the stock tune with downpipe and front pipe.

finding: Dyno numbers only compare on the same dyno and conditions: different dyno types read up to about 30 hp apart; CVT cars lose more through the driveline; KTuner's 10th-gen CVT sheets mismatched rpm at the top end and the Brazilian test car was factory-detuned; in hot, humid climates on RON97 most tuned CVT cars land just under 200 whp.
notes: Supports judging this car only against its own drives at matched intake temperature (kc-heat-soak). civicx-52/89 hot-humid line is a search summary (civicx-89 also claims an unverified 215 hp).

finding: Owner impressions: going 19 to 21 psi is noticeable but 'not a whole new world'; Stage 2 21 psi on a stock CVT is a dramatic change from stock; after a year, drivability and less lag are what owners value most.

DSport's 10th-gen tests: 187 whp at 18.55 psi stock, 197 whp / 218 lb-ft at 23.2 psi on a Hondata calibration, 212.65 whp / 230 lb-ft at 25.56 psi on a custom tune with intake and intercooler: about 2 whp per extra psi at the peak, more torque at 3,000 rpm.
notes: Physics check (stage2/psi_power.py): +1 psi at 20 psi is +2.9 % charge density, at most about +5 whp on about 176 whp, about +2 whp as measured; the hot-vs-cool pair (19.9 vs 16.7 psi) is a 10 % density swing. A Boost step is smaller than a heat-soak difference, so it must be proven on matched Cool pulls. 10th gen (probably Si).

finding: On stock calibration the 1.5T loses power above about 5,500-5,800 rpm (27WON stock Si dyno 189 whp / 195 wtq; owner of a 10th-gen Si); tuned maps pull to about 6,200 rpm.
notes: Si numbers.
